card.name: Words after all or every
card.fires_on: Words that follow a universal quantifier such as all, every, everything or both, often the verb, noun or punctuation right after it. It fits clauses that state something holds for the whole group.

modes.label: Right after all/every
modes.description: The next word after 'all' or 'every' in a sentence that applies to everyone or everything.
modes.example: Practically every building of any size had<< been>> seized by the workers and was draped with

modes.label: Closing a universal claim
modes.description: A word or period that ends a clause stating that all items share a property.
modes.example: All corticosteroids increase calcium excretion<<.>> Patients should not be vaccinated against smallp

modes.label: All of the following
modes.description: Words in a phrase like 'all of the following' that introduces a list of required conditions.
modes.example: Consider dose increases in patients who meet all of the<< following>> conditions: Inadequate efficacy as demonstrated

card.writes: It seems to push toward quantity words and away from 'except', which suits a clause that has no exceptions.
card.plain: It lights up on the words just after 'all' or 'every', where a sentence says something applies to everyone.
